name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3451
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Merlot, fish, and escargot: extremely honorific treatment

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: Merlot is a red wine
a freshwater fish
the first and last letters of escargot

explanation.surface: A lavish French dinner of wine, fish and snails, laid on for an honoured guest.
explanation.walkthrough: The menu reads like the definition of honorific treatment, but each course is just a piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet is the idiom for giving a visitor a ceremonial, VIP welcome.

clue.text: Medium in thin 19A

indicators.note: in places the letter for medium inside the word meaning thin

blocks.note: reedy means thin, like a reed
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue about a medium sitting inside something thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 19 Across, which is CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment that heals, a synonym of cure.

clue.text: Outmoded rule in D&D: "Engaged in mission, harm not a legendary archer"

blocks.note: surface padding that doubles as a hint: the initials of the policy's two halves
to don something is to put it on, to engage in it
a task is an assigned mission
an order not to hurt William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A Dungeons & Dragons rule: on a quest, leave the legendary bowman unharmed.
explanation.walkthrough: D&D looks like Dungeons & Dragons but is the policy's initials. The 1994-2011 US military policy barred openly gay people from serving.
explanation.definitionFit: The policy was repealed in 2011, so it is a rule that is now obsolete.

clue.text: Expression of regret from a disheartened dude, packing shirt

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle of the word is removed
packing something means holding it inside, so the item of clothing goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
a guy with its heart, the middle letter, taken out
a polo is a short-sleeved shirt

explanation.surface: A dejected guy says sorry while stuffing a shirt into his bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Dude means guy, and it is AGY, the A plus the heartless guy, that packs the shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology is a statement saying sorry, the standard expression of regret.

clue.text: Writer that reshaped most of extended sports event

indicators.note: something reshaped is given a new form, so the letters take a new order
most of a word means all but its last letter

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the word that with its letters rearranged
long, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: An author who reworked a long sporting competition, perhaps a novelist rewriting a marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like a person; it is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The pentathlon is an athletic contest of five events, so it is a sports event.

clue.text: How food might be ordered in African country

blocks.note: first meaning: as a takeaway, the American phrase for food to be eaten off the premises
second meaning: the West African republic between Ghana and Benin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests restaurant service somewhere in Africa; split the answer as two words for the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering food 'to go' is the American idiom for takeout, and Togo is a nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Elevate Rex (alt-right requirement)

blocks.note: the letters running from inside Rex into alt
surface padding completing the political picture

explanation.surface: A political jibe: promoting someone called Rex is what the alt-right demands.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis looks like the heart of the clue, but the answer simply sits across the first two words after the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to raise them in rank or praise, a synonym of elevate.

clue.text: Green vine tangled round you and me

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted out of order, so the letters are rearranged
going round something encloses it, so the jumbled letters surround the pronoun

blocks.note: the four letters of vine rearranged, with room left for what goes inside
the pronoun covering you and me

explanation.surface: A garden scene: a green creeper twisted around the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled vine wraps round the pronoun, which sits before its last letter. Green looks like the vine's colour but means jealous.
explanation.definitionFit: Green, as in 'green with envy', is an idiom for jealous or covetous.

clue.text: Victorian novelist and soldier sweeten tart, leaving last piece of pineapple until the end…

indicators.text: leaving last piece of pineapple until the end
indicators.note: leaving one letter till the end takes it out of its place and moves it to the finish

blocks.note: a soldier ant
to honey something is to sweeten it
tart and trollop are both disparaging words for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A recipe: an army cook sweetens a tart, keeping the last pineapple piece for the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The E that ends pineapple is the one moved from the sweetener to the very end. The ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote the Barsetshire and Palliser novels in the reign of Queen Victoria.

clue.text: …subsequently penning enthusiastic review for poem

indicators.note: to pen something in is to enclose it, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: then means afterwards
a rave is a glowing review

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the novelist afterwards writes a glowing review of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the Trollope clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raven is Edgar Allan Poe's famous 1845 narrative poem.

clue.text: Heavy rainfall before long (after Monday)

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for Monday
before long means shortly

explanation.surface: A forecast: a downpour is coming shortly, once Monday is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After Monday' places MON first, with the word for 'before long' following it.
explanation.definitionFit: A monsoon is the seasonal wind that brings torrential rain to South Asia, so heavy rainfall describes it.

clue.text: Historic steps in Georgia decision to imprison head of Teamsters

indicators.note: imprisoning something means locking it inside, so one piece goes within another
the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the US postal code for Georgia
a vote is a decision made by ballot
the opening letter of Teamsters

explanation.surface: A news item about a Georgia ruling that jails a union boss, called a historic step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Historic steps' looks like a comment on the ruling but is the definition: an old dance. The Teamsters are a big American trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is a French court dance of the 17th and 18th centuries, so its steps are historic.

clue.text: Interpreter's mother eaten by fiery beast

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a fire-breathing monster
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A grisly tale in which a translator's mum is swallowed by a dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the interpreter is what the rest of the clue builds.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an official interpreter and guide in Turkish, Arabic and Persian-speaking countries.

clue.text: 5 retreats in Buenos Aires and another South American capital

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the cross-referenced answer is read in the opposite direction
in places the cross-referenced answer inside the letters standing for the city

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for Buenos Aires
the answer to 5 Down

explanation.surface: Something withdraws to Buenos Aires and to a second South American capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Buenos Aires looks like part of the definition, but only its abbreviation is used; the word 'another' acknowledges that it too is a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the capital of Colombia, a second South American capital alongside Buenos Aires.

clue.text: Intend to return, entertaining tip from interesting old hags in island nation

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for intend is read backwards
a host entertaining guests has them inside, so the other pieces go within
the tip of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to aim is to intend
the first letter of interesting
crones are old women, hags

explanation.surface: Someone plans to go back to an island nation to see some fascinating old women.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word splits around its middle, enclosing the initial letter and the old women.
explanation.definitionFit: The Federated States of Micronesia is a Pacific country made up of hundreds of islands.

clue.text: Operator to talk back? Fine

indicators.note: talking back here means the word for talk is read backwards

blocks.note: on American phones you dial 0, read as the letter O, for the operator
to yak is to chatter

explanation.surface: A phone operator asks if it is all right to answer back, and is told that's fine.
explanation.walkthrough: On US phones, dialling zero reaches the operator, so 'Operator' stands for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay and fine are interchangeable words of approval or assent.

clue.text: Laugh at tax collectors trimming back of president's coiffure

indicators.note: trimming cuts something off, and here what is cut is the back, the final letter

blocks.note: the sound of a laugh
the Internal Revenue Service, the US tax authority
John Tyler, tenth US president, without his last letter

explanation.surface: People laugh at the tax men who are cutting a president's hair at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The president is John Tyler, whose name loses its final R; 'at' simply links the laugh to the tax collectors.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiffure is the way someone's hair is arranged, which is a hairstyle.

clue.text: Note in opulent English ballet

indicators.note: in places the musical note inside the word for opulent

blocks.note: swank means showy, luxurious
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A programme note on a lavish English ballet production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English ballet' reads as one phrase, but English gives only a letter; the ballet itself is Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's ballet, one of the most performed in the repertoire.

clue.text: Miscreant rode?

blocks.note: surface reading: a villain who went on horseback
setter's reading: the word rode is a jumble of the letters of the word for one who does, a doer badly rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as WRONG DOER: rode is DOER written wrong, and a wrongdoer is a miscreant.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a person who behaves badly or breaks the law, a synonym of wrongdoer.

clue.text: Fashionable man's arrogance and desire after losing face

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so losing it means the first letter goes

blocks.note: gall is brazen impudence
want, minus its first letter

explanation.surface: A portrait of a dandy whose vanity and longing have left him humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing face' suggests humiliation; it only removes the first letter of the word for desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant, as a noun, is a dashing, stylishly dressed man about town.

clue.text: Mötley Crüe's 1D

indicators.note: motley means mixed and jumbled, so the band name's letters are thrown together anew

blocks.note: the band's name, read without its decorative umlaut

explanation.surface: A nod to the heavy-metal band Mötley Crüe and whatever their remedy might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The band name itself is the clue: its first word tells you to mix up its second.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure and a remedy are both something that heals or puts right an ailment.

clue.text: Pastoral worker spilled chowder

indicators.note: spilled soup ends up in a mess, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmhand knocks over a bowl of chowder.
explanation.walkthrough: Chowder is a thick American fish or clam soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowherd tends cattle at pasture, so is a worker in the pastoral, rural sense.

clue.text: In atlas, we described natives of Scandinavia

indicators.note: In says the answer is sitting inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of atlas, all of we and the start of described

explanation.surface: We wrote about Scandinavian people in an atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Described' looks like the verb of the sentence, but its first three letters complete the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are the people of Sweden, one of the Scandinavian countries.

clue.text: In retrospect, felt tense grasping prickly plant

indicators.note: the words hold the target between them, grasping it within their letters
looking back means the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of felt and the start of tense

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being on edge while gripping a thorny plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt tense' looks like a definition of an emotion; it is only the string of letters that hides the plant written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nettle is a plant whose stinging hairs prick the skin; the clue's 'prickly' covers that sting.

clue.text: Reduce speed, pulling in immediately at center of Aspen!

definitions.text: Reduce speed, pulling in immediately at center of Aspen!

indicators.note: pulling something in brings it inside, so the following pieces go within the first word
the center of a five-letter word is its third, middle letter

blocks.note: to slow is to reduce speed
now means at once
the middle letter of Aspen

explanation.surface: A road warning in the Colorado ski town of Aspen: slow down and pull over now.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the machine: a slow vehicle pulling in at the center of a snowy Aspen road. SNOWPLOW is the US spelling of snowplough.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowplow is a slow-moving vehicle that clears snow from roads, the kind that makes traffic reduce speed in a ski town.

clue.text: 14 beginners in yoga exercise at home

indicators.note: beginners are the starting letters of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Four starting moves in a yoga workout done in your living room.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 14 Across, OKAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is an informal yes, the same assent as okay.

clue.text: Say, "To get old is ordinary"

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone declares that growing old is nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress up a charade: the verb for saying, then the verb for getting old.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means typical or unremarkable, a synonym for ordinary.

clue.text: Heavenly body rejecting a drug

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it out, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a small rocky body orbiting the sun
taken as written; this is the letter rejected

explanation.surface: A celestial body turns down a drug, or a beautiful athlete refuses doping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' could suggest a gorgeous physique, tempting a sporting reading; it is a space rock that loses its opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: A steroid is a class of drug, notably the anabolic kind used to build muscle.

clue.text: Brilliant success when white powder and ecstasy make a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the combined letters are read back the other way

blocks.note: talc is a white powder
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug story: a triumph when cocaine and ecstasy return to the party scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White powder' suggests cocaine, but it is the harmless kind used on babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is a French borrowing for dazzling success or brilliant effect.

clue.text: Covering that man at 1600 Pennsylvania Ave., for example

blocks.note: the pronoun for that man
1600 Pennsylvania Avenue is the White House's street address

explanation.surface: A cover story about the man who lives at the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'for example' marks the street location as one instance of the category word.
explanation.definitionFit: A headdress is a covering worn on the head, often ornamental or ceremonial.
